reviews.title: A frustrating disappointment
reviews.text:
I grew up on these games as a child and I came back to toca nature for a quick nostalgia fix. Yes, I know that app wasn’t free, much like a lot of toca apps, but I was willing to pay for it for what it was worth. What I am not willing to do is pay for the entire interface by itself. I downloaded this new app only to find everything is locked behind a paywall. That is crazy for kids games. 

Respectfully, this new app is not only NOT worth it, but a scam and a way to take advantage of the new generation of changing media. Bring back the old apps. Bring back the apps without ads, paywalls, pops, and bring back our childhood so that this generation can grow up with the games i enjoyed.

reviews.title: weird description & lore
reviews.text: so on the app logo it looks normal, right? there’s a woman (from kitchen 2) and the bunny from the pet doctor. but if you look at the woman’s neck, it’s blue. this is a signal of choking and needs medical help and attention, mind you, 6 year old me (a few years ago) thought that she must’ve just been at the hair salon and dye and/or pigment slipped underneath her neck for some reason, and i connected it with other clues i found in the game. after around 15-20 minutes of playing, i found a picture of her nearby, with DUCT TAPE covering her mouth, but there wasn’t much else. i found videos on youtube talking about something similar happening in the game, in fact, the longer they actually played, the more lore and understanding you got. i would really rather not get this game, because kitchen 2 is kinda boring and kinda reminds me of being kidnapped, if you will. but the other games are fun, however, you have to PAY for them, which is just pointless and there’s no way my parents will get the full access for me, mainly because the price is FOR SURE gonna take a toll on their savings for groceries, water, cat and dog food, etc. remove the weird backstory and lore please! it really makes me grossed out, especially over a KIDS game, and i have a bad fear of being outside at night past my car and mailbox, because i’m worried about being kidnapped.

reviews.title: What?!?
reviews.text: I’ve noticed a change in toca boca games, there is a new developer, Piknik. Ever since piknik became the developer/owner of these games it has been feeling like my own childhood was ripped away from me. Toca boca games no longer feel the same. I’ve played this toca boca jr game and it still has the same old games i used to play, but buried behind a padlock. Toca Boca Jr is an extremely greedy game taking your money through a subscription. I’ve noticed that same pattern with Piknik games like Sago Mini World. Sago Mini World has the same problem as Toca Boca Jr. It wants all your money and disguises it through a subscription. They’ve also destroyed all the old Toca Boca games. I’ve noticed my favorites were gone from the App Store. Those individual games are better than Toca Boca Jr because you only had to pay for it once and you could play it forever, but now they are all torn away from you and the only way to unlock them is by paying a subscription that you have to pay monthly. Shame on you, both Toca Boca and Piknik.

reviews.title: You have to purchase everything!
reviews.text:
Only one out of the sixteen games is free. To be completely Frank? It's ridiculous! This game is for kids, and it shouldn't be completely locked behind a paywall. 

I can understand that it is still an appropriate game for children that might entertain them temporarily. However, it’s not as fun as it claims to be in the long run. You can only access one game, which is very basic. It gets dull and repetitive. 

I’m not saying that everything in the game needs to be free. The company needs to make money, after all. Still, I believe you would improve the app a lot by offering at least six free games. This isn’t even half of what’s available, but it would really enhance the app! Don’t waste your time on this app until they fix the excessive paywalls.

reviews.title: Make this more accessible
reviews.text: As a parent, I’m disappointed that only one Toca Boca game is free while the rest require a monthly subscription. My child absolutely loves these games, so it’s hard having to say no when they want to explore more content. While I understand companies need to make money, a subscription can feel limiting for families. It would be great to see more free options or a one-time purchase instead, so more children can enjoy the games without ongoing costs.
